newsitem.title: USA: DEC sues Intel, seeks "huge" compensation.
newsitem.headline: DEC sues Intel, seeks "huge" compensation.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp said Tuesday it was seeking a "huge" damage award in its patent infringement suit against Intel Corp.
DEC Chief Executive Office Robert Palmer declined to specify how much money DEC was seeking but said the compensation figure was "substantial" and that the "numbers involved are quite huge."
Palmer spoke in a conference call with analysts and reporters.
DEC's suit against the world's largest semiconductor maker alleges Intel has infringed 10 Digital patents, using Digital technology to produce the Pentium family of microprocessors.
A spokeswoman for Intel said the company would have no immediate comment on the suit but that executives were evaluating it.
DEC general counsel Thomas Siekman told reporters the company hoped to move the litigation "as quickly as possible" and was prepared to budget whatever was required to pursue its claims.

Analyst Gary Helmig of Soundview Financial said, "I bet this never goes to court. Neither side would want this to go to litigation. It would be very prolonged...At some point, one would expect there would be a counterclaim by Intel."
